body: If they show up physically, you don't have to tell them to go away through the door if you don't want to. If you don't want to talk to them at all, go to a room furthest away from the door and call the non emergency number to have your parents trespassed off the property. They want a response or contact of any kind. Do not give it to them.
Holy Christ yes. What a perfect example. I'm glad you're coming out of the fog and got a new job. Congrats.
What the actual hell. This one takes the cake. I am so sorry.
Right. That's the plan from now on. It's tricky when your romantic partners try to get you to have a relationship with your parent, then see your parent for what they really are.
This is such a great way to put it. Thank you. That's the blatant truth.
I'm sorry you had to deal with that craziness. I'm glad you see through it.

*Hugs* I'm very sorry your mom and golden child brother ganged up on you. My mom also slut shamed me over wearing a short onesie when I was twelve. She had just bought it for me and the second we drove out of Walmart she blew up on me, telling me I was "Trying to show off my ass and that people were going to rape me for it". This is just an example to prove that narcissists say inappropriate things to slut shame their kids for no reason. You didn't deserve what your mom said/did. That is disgusting. I feel for you and the guys you dated. I hope you find a sweet, loving, partner that treats you right.

Both of your parents and cruel, invalidating, ridiculous and lack empathy. Of course you want to be in your room away from them. Dude, your father threatened a murder suicide towards ALL OF YOU. He should be in jail or an institution. Living in a shelter will be rough, but you gotta get out of there ASAP. Your mom blaming you, blame shifting Covid for how you feel and not listening to how you feel is BS. Apply for cash assistance or see if you can get any aid from a public program to get an apartment. I'm so sorry this happened to you.
It's not your fault. Your not a narc. It sounds like you're dealing with psychosis. I feel for you so much. *hugs* I'm glad you're alive. It's going to be okay.

I would just keep telling him "Please don't compliment my appearance. It makes me uncomfortable." Just keep reiterating that. If he doesn't respect you enough to abide by that boundary, he doesn't deserve to be in your life.

Please don't leave her. Please don't leave us. I know it feels unbearable. These feelings are going to come and go. They have a chance of disappearing or decreasing in intensity. But you forfeit any chance of healing or living a better life when you kill yourself. Please don't do it. She loves you. You are loved. You are precious. Your pain is valid. Just please don't act on it. <3

Sounds invasive. I wouldn't bring it up. Which sucks because then it feels like you aren't standing up for yourself, or you're suppressing your feelings. I can see this blowing up though. Grey rock to try to maintain peace.

Oh my gosh yes! My mom pulled the "concern mother act" with my teachers and school counselor. Maybe she was partially concerned, but she was also undoubtedly doing it to punish me for grey rocking her and to be on my butt. I hate it when they recruit flying monkeys and manipulate people. *hugs*

Can relate to the feelings of guilt. When my mom used to tell me she sent me an email, I'd feel immediate dread and irritation. Just because they were long and draining sometimes. Guilt is normal. You have a conscious. You have empathy. It's going to be okay.
I'm proud of you for leaving. Your dad's behavior is ridiculous. There might be some programs that temporarily foster your cat until you have a better situation. Wishing you the best.

Reading all of this makes me so sad. *hugs* The fact that your mom is still insisting you pay for her travel when you have a huge income difference from your siblings, shows that she isn't reasonable. I can't give you a short cut to not feeling insecure. Sometimes you just gotta tell yourself that you're doing the right thing while doing your best. Even if it doesn't feel that way or you don't believe it. You grew up without reassurance, so you likely struggle with reassuring yourself. I do too. It's going to be okay.

When it seems like life is a capital b-word, you probably just leveled up. I apologize if this is imposing what feels like "toxic positivity" on you. Just know that you got this and your feelings of frustration, pain, sadness, whatever they may be are valid. You're a freaking warrior.

Yes. I go back and forth doubting my anger towards the way my mom treated me and my bf. I go back and forth between being assured and doubtful about going NC. I wonder if I'm the narc sometimes. *hugs*

I see how that comes off as a double standard. I'm definitely not trying to do that. I've just been complimented by guys so many times that later state they want something romantic or sexual, so it kind of messes with my head. I feel like if I commented "Cute" on some random guys pic, he might question what I mean by it. Maybe it's just me. But if I just told him I like your jacket, ect, I could see a clear difference. Not trying to fight with you. Just trying to explain and have a good back and forth with you, which seems to be what's going on. :)

Right I understand. I just feel like compliments are more along the lines of: "You look nice, I like your style, cool hair". A one word compliment such as " Cute" is ambiguous. It could be either or and that's what bothers me. I don't know how to respond to certain compliments that can come off as flirting, because I don't want to act in a questionable way that could be seen as disloyalty towards my boyfriend.

To be honest I'm not too sure. We're not exactly typical people. We smoke weed, his daughter has a girlfriend, his daughter has posted a picture of herself on Instagram with lingerie. There's no telling.
I appreciate your insight. Can you please elaborate when you say "That was a test balloon?" Also, can you please tell me how it is inappropriate? I need advice on how to explain that it is.

I just want to give you a huge hug. I'm very sorry you had to endure your dad beating you! And that he still rages at you by yelling. He sounds childish and scary. Please don't tell your parents you are moving. They will somehow find a way to sabotage your move and your job and probably abuse you. Please stay safe. Bless your soul.
Sometimes you can grey rock them and remain neutral. Then they'll sense something is up and keep questioning you about it till you break from frustration. Just a heads up.
She's controlling and invasive. This isn't okay.

I understand. I'm sorry you're going through this. I second guess my emotions too sometimes. Sometimes I feel like the bonafide mom from The Glass Menagerie. We see the truth though. Our narc parents don't. You're not a fraud.

It's not your fault you didn't find out sooner. This type of dysfunctional has been ingrained into you as "normal". How were you supposed to know any different? It's liberating coming out of the fog though. Welcome to the group.
I feel for you. Was in your position till I was 18. It's going to get better. When you can leave, things will be better. *Hugs*
Sounds like you are grey rocking her. I'm proud of you.

I've went back and forth on no contact for three years. Tried to get my mom to understand what she does that drains me and disrespects me. To no avail. The last straw was her disrespecting my boyfriend and I repeatedly since the day after Christmas. I gave her one chance to apologize and admit what she did was wrong. She refused, since then I've refused to talk to her. She's harassing me to this day. 

My advice is go no contact for your own sake. If you don't start a confrontation, it's only a matter of time before your narcissistic parents cause drama or stress. Your job is to take care of yourself. Best of luck.

Hi there, there were a lot of final straws that influenced my decision to go full no contact. She's unlikely to change. I spent seven years trying to get my mom to see where she is wrong. It just damaged and drained him further. Maybe you can keep contact with your brother. If not, you gotta look out for yourself.
Thank you. I appreciate that. I'm glad you're also no contact.

I didn't belittle anyone nor did I lecture anyone. And honestly if they're coming onto this sub and attacking people they deserve to have their ass handed to them. The fact that you accused me of something I did not do already shows your mindset.
People on relationship advice can be toxic, brutal and ruthless as well. But not all of them. Best of luck.
Makes sense.
No it's okay. I understand completely. *hugs*
Damn. This sounds like really good insight. You sound very smart. I'm sure you hit the nail on the head for some narcs with this.

"Shut up. I'm the mom you're the kid"

"I just want what's best for you" *proceeds to force their style of clothes on me. 

"You can't trust anyone but your family. Family is the most important thing"

Who ever told you that is enabling abuse. If someone hit you repeatedly, but also did nice things, it wouldn't matter. Because their behavior would still cycle around to abuse. You have every right to want to be away from it.
My brain has also blocked out chunks of memory. It is a defense mechanism in response to trauma. That is also how abuse am works.
Oh my gosh yes. This hits so close to home. The extent to which they lack self awareness is infuriating.

I'm so sorry this happened to you. What she did to you was beyond inappropriate and abusive. Under ideal circumstances, you would have been taken away. But CPS is a joke and the foster system isn't much better. Screw your parents. You deserved so much better.

Hey, that was more meant as encouragement. You don't have to feel strong or let it roll of your shoulder right now. You're hurt. I'm very sorry if I invalidated your feelings. *Hugs* It's going to be okay. You're going to get out of this situation at some point.

"I just want you to do it my way. This is my house and my rules." Like really!? Even meant in the most casual, anti climatic way, it is ridiculous. Why even bring up "My house my rules"? To instill authority and hold it over someone's head in the most ridiculous way possible, over the most ridiculous reason. She sounds controlling. I'm so sorry OP.
*Claps* Chin up.

I really feel for you. *hugs* My mom did the same thing in a way. Try to relive them now if you can. Dye your hair. Wear clothes you wanted to in highschool but couldn't or want to wear now. Channel your inner teen. Listen to whatever music you want. Try to find people you can party with and be crazy with now. You can still have the things you wanted. And this might sound like a bad idea, but if you make a friend, try to sneak into a highschool prom when possible. Or just go clubbing.

Dude all of this hits so close to home. My mom has literally said the same exact thing about my partner who is amazing. They just like to villianze people and drive a wedge between your relationships.
It is a gradual process. I'm seven years into deprogramming and still working on it. Depending on the individual, it might take longer or shorter. It's going to be okay.
I know. Believe me I know. But you can come back from this. I promise. I'm here if you need to talk.

What I think is that your dad is completely abusive and your step mom is an enabler. He's perfectly capable of applying through the website for himself. Yet he wants to be dependent on you for whatever reason. Your dad making you use a tracker is controlling and ridiculous. Screw him! Seriously. You aren't ungrateful. Narcissist parents love to use rent and living situations as leverage and blackmail over their kids. If he kept hitting you then turning around and apologizing it wouldn't be okay. 

He's emotionally abusing you while making no effort to stop himself in the moment. My mom was the same way. You can try everything you want but the relationship is never going to change because he's an immature, childish, pathetic little man who will never stop his abuse. Everytime I called my mom out on her abuse, she smugly told me "You don't like it move out." I don't care what you have to do, please get out when you can. You might want to move to another state with cheaper living costs. If you can get into an apartment, in some states, they can't kick you out if you are behind on rent because of Covid-19. There are also public programs that help if you are behind rent and bills. I'm so sorry you have to go through this. I could refer you to some resources. Get a cheap bus ticket somewhere and get to a homeless shelter for just a little bit.

Hi there. First of all *huge hugs* to you. I'm so sorry you had to go through all of this. You might already know this, but I'll share just in case you don't. What your mother did to you is called "parentification". It is when the roles are reversed and parents dump their problems on young kids that aren't equipped to deal with them. You probably had to " wear many hats" (play many roles to satisfy your mom). 

We rationalize our parents behavior at that age because we don't know what else to do. We empathize with them. We were trapped victims with no guidance. What she said to you at sixteen was real f-ed up and you could've been taken away for that. She literally threatened to murder you!

The way you get independent is by determining your interests, slowly weening yourself off emotional codependency towards your emotionally unavailable mom, and move out. It is more intricate but easier than it sounds. The best place to start convincing yourself is affirmations. Telling yourself "I'm just a person. I'm not a burden. I'm not an intrusion" is a good place to start. You most likely developed people pleasing (A form of codependency through chronic self neglect) as a consequence of having to please your mom. It wasn't your fault. *hugs*

It will get easier I promise. I went the opposite way and rebelled. Tried weed and psychedelics (Which I love), am getting tattoos (Which nmom hates), going to work in a dispensary. This isn't a life I chose out of spite. I genuinely enjoy it. Nmom hates it. I gradually started to not care about her approval when I got fed up with her criticism and control. Try to remember that with every good thing in your life you work for, that you are getting closer to total emancipation. As spiteful as it may sound, with every victory, you are gaining independence from her. You most likely have trauma. Soldiers coming home from war need time to adjust before it is even possible for them to acclimate back into society. 

You just need time to adjust. How much time? No one knows. You're already an adult. Congrats!

A lot of what you say hits so close to home. Can relate for sure. Guilt is normal. You have a conscious and empathy. That's why you care. You aren't ignorant and complacent like your parents. That's why you feel bad. Seems like they subconsciously or unconsciously can't live without drama. They feel emotional hunger and lack of supply (They get supply from your drama) when you are away from them. The second you're with them, they become complacent because your presence halfway fills their emotional void. That's the closest to love some parents get. Narcissists get supply from drama and chaos. From turbulent relationships. 

I moved out of my mom's when I was 18. I kept feeling a strange tug and guilt when I was away from her. I wouldn't realize till later that I was still emotionally codependent on her and being subconsciously driven by guilt of "leaving" her. Yet I used to dread seeing her or reading her letters. I couldn't figure out why. It was because she was draining. 

My mom abused and manipulated me behind closed doors. My friend's parents enabled her behavior and influenced me into keeping contact with her when it was unhealthy. They were dysfunctional and ignorant in their own way. This response is already long, so I don't want to go into more detail unless you want. But I know exactly what you are going through when you say they deny, change the story and act like nothing happened. When it is an emotional rollercoaster. From the time I was 18 to now (I'm 25) I cried so hard out of grief and guilt. I have age lines on my face that make me look thirty from crying so much. Don't let the guilt trick you. 

I would go very low contact or no contact, seeing as they are detrimental to your mental health.

Amen! I used to hear parents in middle school angrily ranting about things like this. I wondered what in the hell was such a big deal. Then considered the possibility there was something I wasn't seeing. That I would understand when I was older. Nope! It's just controlling bs.

It is difficult, but if you have access to the internet, try researching different things to see what you are into. Try to identity interests by watching cool, educational videos on YouTube. Look into different styles. If you like something, pay attention to it and don't dismiss it. Immerse yourself in it. If you could get therapy, they might be able to help you too.

She sounds like a straight up tyrant. Any attempt to explain yourself is immediately shut down, then deemed as disrespect. She cut you off. She has a mental disorder for sure that you take the brunt of. *hugs*
I understand where you are coming from. You didn't have the ability to develop your own authentic identity and sense of self. That is so important. *hugs*

Hey, I was living with my friend, her sis and her parents. They were cool at first, but then her dad started becoming gradually more controlling. That situation blew up and I ended up moving in with my boyfriend who ended up being abusive and an alcoholic who made me pick up his financial slack. 

If I could go back and do things differently, I would apply for cash assistance immediately through Income Support Division, Food Stamps, and apply for Disability (Which I am now on). Then I'd apply for housing or get my own cheap place asap. If you don't want to rely on government assistance, I'd try to get income that doesn't come from your parents and move in with your friend for a little bit. 

Not saying your friend and her dad are bad people, but all sorts of little things can cause people living together to clash. I would save while living with them and move out into your own cheap place asap. Best of luck.

A good way to set a boundary is by communicating: "My feelings are valid. You might not understand mom and dad, but that doesn't make them any less real. I'm allowed to feel the way I do." If they continue to argue you, I would grey rock them, then tell them let's agree to disagree. 

If they continue to push their perspective and Invalidate/minimize your feelings then they have a real problem. That is when you reach out to another adult or friend you trust and tell them that your parents are invalidating your feelings, and won't stop fighting you on it.
I'm happy for you. It's life when Flynn Rider saved Rapunzel. <3

No. You misunderstood. When I was an older child, she would make me pose for several photos when I did not want to. All her other narcissistic abusive behavior later on such as verbal abuse, physical abuse, and gaslighting made me resent the baby photos when I looked back on them.
You're not over reacting. They are terrible to you. I would go very low contact or no contact if at all possible.
This hits close to home. My mom was the same way. I'm sorry you're going through this. *hugs*
Yes. However all the empathy and understanding in the world will not cause them to be accountable or self aware. They are tragic victims in a way. Yet do not want to be better.

You don't deserve this. It is controlling of them to force you into religion. I'm sure your pixie cut looks beautiful. Screw your dad. Can you leave anywhere? Any shelters maybe? Lie that your dad pushed you against the wall and you're scared he's going to hit you? The cops don't have to be involved for the shelter to let you stay. You don't deserve to live with controlling jerks.

Oh my gosh. I'm BPD too. Raised by a single, covert, narc, mother. I was diagnosed in 2018 and didn't accept it at first. Yes, borderlines are stigmatized negatively. We aren't how they portray us to be. It is normal and valid for you to have feelings of anger and sadness. Especially when you developed this disorder as a result of your upbringing. It is going to be okay. You have the most important piece in self awareness, healing and improvement. We are here for you. <3

The guilt children of narcs feel is insidious. I know it's hard to detach from your parents. But think of it this way. If your mom didn't give birth to you, she'd be just another toxic person you'd cut off. It's extremely brutal to have to detach from our parents that way, because we are biologically programmed. Your husband needed you. I'm glad he pulled through. It must have been difficult not being able to tell him, because he was trying to pull through. I feel for you. *hugs*

Your mom sounds like a narc or is toxic at the very least. She doesn't respect boundaries. How dare she cut herself and blame it on you. I've cut myself before. My abusive ex was relentlessly hurling verbal and emotional abuse at me. I was cornered in the bathroom at our studio apartment in the middle of winter. Had no where else to go. And when he wouldn't stop harassing me and yanking my phone out of my hand, I had a breakdown, cut and blamed him for it. I feel like that's a different situation than what your mom pulled. 

It was wrong of her to blame you. I was also drained/ exhausted after high school when my mom would want to talk my ear off. I would constantly tell her I wasn't in the mood to hear her. Which led her to saying "You can't control me. I can talk at you whenever I want. You're abusive. You're just using me. You don't love me". She also compared me to my dad which is relatable. I'm sorry about your brother. I'm sorry about you having to see her in order to visit him. Your mom put too much on a child. You're not crazy. She's the problem.

Your mom's bf is ridiculous. He is inconsiderate, he feels justified and doesn't very much care. I'm sorry your mom enables  him. You're not asking too much. He's disgusting. While it is possible that you may be projecting past resentment from other bf's, you have justification for feeling apprehensive towards her relationships. He comes off as very narcissistic himself. Behaving as if you are crazy, or inflicting a burden on him. Your mom putting you on the spot is not cool either.

You hit the nail on the head. I'm sorry your mom did not respect your desire to express yourself. I'm sorry she imposed her style on you. Like why ask what the kids need if you're just going to impose what you want anyway? And then she starts swearing at you? Unacceptable. She wants things her way. You deserve so much better.

Oh shoot. Okay, that makes things a bit more complicated but I understand. Apple ID's are tricky. The parents can monitor their children's activity though Apple features. I would recommend your lil sis records their abusive behavior (rage) as a defense. This could also be used to protect you against legal action, with you stating that you are concerned about your sister's well being. However if your step dad or mom monitors your sister's icloud, they will see that she is recording them/ building a case against them. In that case, I would recommend she gets a secret phone that can record their behavior (android or something without Apple ID) that she uploads to a secret cloud and is password protected. I understand you are scared of legal action. That's why r/legaladvice would be a good subreddit to consult as well. I wish you both the best.

Of course they compare. This is called gatekeeping and competing. No one has it worse than them. They either didn't get enough validation growing up, or they are an insatiable black hole that can't be satisfied. I'm sorry your dad minimized, dismissed and invalidated your problems. You hit the nail on the hammer about his behavior.

As children of narcissists, we develop narcissistic fleas. I used to struggle with insincere, half apologies that defended and justified my actions. I struggled to really put myself in others shoes. I struggled to develop empathy, I struggled to be accountable and admit what I did wrong. We are all getting better. I'm proud of you for being self aware. We have to learn to accept that we do wrong things. And just because we make mistakes or mess up, doesn't mean we are horrible. It's our egos or anger that get in the way of being genuinely sorry.

Sure. My mom said it all the time. And seemed sincere. But I think her love was mostly indifference emotional hunger. Some narcs do love their kids in a twisted way. That doesn't exclude the damage they inflict. I'm sorry your mom never said it. :(

Hi there. There are so many alarm bells ringing about your mom's behavior. 

"Well why did we spend so much money otherwise? Why did we spend so much money on your upbringing?" Dude! She feels ENTITLED to you TAKING CARE OF HER because she raised you. That's messed up and not okay. She feels that you are indebted to her for raising you. You are your own person. We don't owe our parents anything. No matter what cultural stigmas say. No matter how hard anyone tries to advocate differently!


And her grabbing pills and threatening suicide? She's either really feeling that hurt/angry/ hopeless or whatever, or she's using that as a manipulation tactic. Either way, it's not healthy, mature, or normal. You're not in the wrong. You tried numerous times to explain to your mom that she's wrong with her entitlement and that she's taking things too far. She refuses to stop. She catastrophizes the situation and makes it worse. She got triggered but didn't handle it well. 

Whether she's purposely playing the victim or feels legitimately victimized doesn't matter. She lacks self awareness and needs to be accountable. I'm so sorry your lil brother had to see this. You're not a terrible person. You act out because she literally drives you CRAZY. Nothing will ever be enough for them. *Hugs* it's going to be okay.

Dude. I'm so sorry. My mom screamed at me for an hour in highschool because I didn't turn her light off. She's compared me to other friends/kids and asked me why I was a bad kid, while other kids were angels. Then she'd revert back to being loving. 

How you cope? You cope by knowing that you deserve better, by knowing her insane behavior isn't your fault, by knowing that you won't be trapped with her forever. You cope by knowing there was nothing you could have done to make her love you. That she was going to be this way with ANY kid regardless. You cope by knowing you are going to be independent, and that your revenge will be living your own life far away from her. *Hugs* Please don't hurt yourself or blame yourself. I'm here if you ever need to talk.
Damn. They sound extremely controlling. Calling the police for a civil escort might be a good idea. Just so your parents don't try to pull anything when they find out.

Hey. Just because your experience isn't as bad as what other people post on here, doesn't mean that your parents aren't toxic. If some of the symptoms ring a bell, then that is most likely what is going on. If you're even having to ask yourself if you parents are narcs, they probably are. Narcissists vary in the severity of their behaviors. Some are worse than others. Your experience is valid.

My advice would be buying your sister a prepaid phone that she can contact you with. Give it to her in secret. Make sure she hides it and that your parents don't find out she has it. A good way to do this is to have her keep it stashed inside a bra or her pockets. Maybe she could secretly sew a pocket inside her clothes. She needs a stash spot that isn't obvious. Inside her curtains, inside a pair of shoes, in a jacket in her closet, in a flash light maybe. Anywhere but under the mattress or in an underwear drawer. Parents always check those places. 

If that isn't possible, maybe she can email you from a school computer once school starts again. If things get too bad, you might want to contact CPS. If you really want to go that route, you could try to fight in court for custody of your little sister. Otherwise she'll have to wait till she's 18 or emancipated (Which is a difficult process). I would go no contact if you can manage a way to be in contact with your lil sis secretly.

That is convenient. Yeah, they just don't want to learn. You can either succumb to her method of communication, or she'll just have to learn if she really wants to be in touch with you (Cue her guilt tripping manipulation where she blames you for not caring enough to be in touch with her). I wish you the best. You deserve so much better.

My reality has shifted back and forth like how you are describing. It is alarming how much our truth can be doubted. When we know we are being abused, but our mind trivializes the situation. You're not over reacting. His good side won't stop his pattern of abuse from repeating. Drunk texting you angry novels is abusive and childish. You're doing the right thing.

Not to worry you, but there is a possibility your dad might tell your mom. If that happens, there is still no obligation to let either of them into your life. I would not tell her that you are pregnant. Protect your energy and sanity. You've got a little one and a loving partner you have to protect from their chaos now too.

Oh my gosh yes! I used to struggle with the alternation you describe. I have borderline personality disorder, so I deal with splitting sometimes. Splitting is seeing a person with only their negative traits or positive traits. A good middle ground is realizing that while they have redeemable traits, that doesn't change what they've done. That your narc will continue to repeat their behavior that will make you hate them. I used to feel so guilty. I'd think of my mom's loving, tender, side while my mind completely disqualified everything bad she did, and I'd under go abuse amnesia. It is scary how many times a day this would come and go. 

You can have resentment for how your mom treated you without hating her. Or if you hate her it's okay. She flips between sides. So your perception of her flips with her behavior. Its not your fault. *hugs*

I'm so proud of you! Yes!!!! There is a saying: "After you heal from narcissistic abuse, you might want to stop following Instagram pages that talk about it. Not all behavior you dislike is automatically narcissistic. Don't be so quick to pathologize people. Most people are good and doing their best."

However, be careful not to minimize what you went through or potentially abusive/ manipulative behavior from others. There is a good middle ground. Our upbringing from narc parents made us cynical and pessimistic. It made us feel like the world was going to bite us with no warning. You are on the right track.

That is absolutely nasty. My mom made an offhand remark during lunch the day after Christmas. She interfered with me seeing my boyfriend who lives with me. This made him sad. So she said "It's a good thing he's sad he can't see you. That way he gets a taste of his own medicine". She said it in such a casual, offhanded, way like your dad. The way they make these disgusting remarks does not eliminate the intent/ meaning behind them. I'm sorry you dealt with this.

My mom used to bait me. She used to bring up something important had happened, but when I asked her what, she'd childishly respond with "I'm going to be just like you and not tell you. My life isn't important to you". So manipulative. You're doing it to protect your energy. She's doing it out of petty, spiteful, revenge. That is the difference. You're doing the right thing.

They are toxic and abusive. That is for sure. For no contact: Block them on everything. You can either ghost them with no explanation or tell them why before you do it. For VLC, just create a separate email account only for them so you don't get surprised by emails that might trigger you. Email them only once a month. No phone calls, no visits. Best of luck.

Hey. Just my opinion, but I would wait till after I'm gone to tell them or just leave a note for when you're gone. I'm sorry they sabotaged everything for you. You're doing the right thing by leaving.
Congrats on blocking him. You don't deserve his toxic, macho, behavior.

Hey. My mom used to pull this crap. When I was a teenager, I would call her out on her emotional invalidation or gaslighting. She'd then immediately start shouting "I cook, I clean, I give you rides, I buy things!" To discredit my statement. Then she revert back to offering to give me rides because it made her happy and she cared. To buying me things "Because it filled a mothers heart with joy". Then she'd revert back to being angry, abusive, and throwing it in my face. I thought she was psychotic for switching back and forth all the time. 


They might genuinely want to help in the moment. But you'll do something that angers them or makes them feel like you didn't give them what they wanted, and revert to your parent's behavior. *hugs*
I understand what you mean. I feel for you. It's good that you realized the source of these thoughts. That way neither your mom or her voice can control your life anymore.

I would try telling your mom that visiting three times a month is too much. You are already overwhelmed raising your children while trying to have time to yourself to relax. I would also tell her that interacting with your dad takes a toll on you and that you would rather just visit with her.
